newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fabre-Domergue group plans Martinique cocoa plant.
newsitem.headline: Fabre-Domergue group plans Martinique cocoa plant.

text.p: The French Caribbean-based Fabre Domergue group plans to set up a cocoa beans processing plant in the island of Martinique, company officials said on Wednesday.

The plant located on the Atlantic coast of the island will initially produce an annual 1,000 tonnes of high-quality cocoa paste mainly destined for Europe. The remainder will go to the U.S. markets, project manager Jean-Luc Pierre told Reuters.
Capacity may later be raised to 4,000 tonnes if needed, he added. Investment costs are estimated at around 15 million francs for equipment.
From January 1998 the plant will process an estimated 1,200 tonnes of cocoa beans, imported from the Caribbean zone and from Venezuela, he said.
The paste is destined to meet growing demand from chocolate makers for high quality products, he said.

The group is already negotiating with Venezuela and other producers long-term supply contracts at fixed prices guaranteeing top quality beans and sheltering supplies from price fluctuations on international world cocoa markets.
The Fabre Domergue group has assets in real estate, tourism and banana growing. It had sales of 760 million francs in 1996.
